title: Euro symbol appears on Quick Accent after the update 100
author: alexpf

status.label: Handled by linked trackers
status.detail: A Quick Accent collaborator identified the alphabetical character-set ordering change and linked #50099 for custom set priority plus #25217 for frequency-ordering failures.

next_action.label: Follow existing trackers
next_action.reason: The current thread already contains the product explanation and canonical follow-up issues; no additional dashboard comment or design is needed.

judgment.rationale: Maintainer discussion has separated the report into two existing workstreams: configurable language/set ordering in #50099 and incorrect frequency sorting in #25217.
evidence: A collaborator explained that German and Spanish have long included €, while alphabetical set ordering changed the first character from é to €.
The reporter prefers stable, user-controlled language priority rather than frequency-based movement.
Collaborator daverayment opened and linked #50099 for custom ordering of character sets.
The later report that frequency sorting leaves € first was linked to #25217.
judgment.recommended_action: Expose no new action; retain this issue as handled by #50099 and #25217 and let the existing collaborator-owned discussion proceed.

issue_context.summary: After Quick Accent changed built-in character-set ordering to alphabetical, € appears before é for users selecting German and Spanish; frequency sorting also reportedly fails to restore the preferred order.
known_information: German contributes € on E and Spanish contributes é and €; the symbols were not newly added in 0.100.
The ordering change from source declaration order to alphabetical language order explains the visible priority change.
The reporter does not want positions to float with usage frequency and instead wants configurable language priority.
Open #50099 tracks custom ordering of character sets, and open #25217 tracks frequency sorting not working.
inferences: The original report combines a deliberate ordering-policy change with a potentially separate persistence/sorting bug, rather than one root-cause defect.
issue_context.analysis: The complete discussion already contains maintainer explanation, ownership, and canonical follow-up links. The earlier actionable-design classification is no longer current because the work is split and tracked elsewhere.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, all six comments, labels, timeline, linked PR #48489, and linked issue #50099.
PR #48489 attempted to remove € from German/Spanish mappings but was closed with changes requested and not merged.
Inspected CharacterMappings.cs and tests: built-in display order is explicitly alphabetical; PowerAccent.cs contains the usage-frequency sorting path.
Confirmed #50099 and #25217 remain open and directly cover the two requested outcomes.
